heading: Conception of existence
english: “The conception of existence is immediate [not acquired through demonstration].”
note: The two words of this lemma straddle printed pages I:33–34. The running explanation treats the statement “a thing is either existent or nonexistent” as presupposing intelligible concepts of existence and nonexistence. The commentary should not be made to imply that all ontological doctrines are self-evident.
evidence: DIRECT PRINTED IMAGE — candidate matn lemma; independently collate with Tahdhīb before textual certification

heading: Complete efficient causation and the effect
category: Quoted matn embedded in running commentary
arabic: (وعند تمام الفاعل) بجميع جهات التأثير من الشرائط والآلات والقابل (يجب وجود المعلول)، فإنه لو جاز عدمه لكان وجوده بعد ذلك ترجيحاً بلا مرجح
english: “When the producing cause is complete”—with respect to every determinant of its operation, including its conditions, instruments and receptive subject—“the effect must exist”; for if its nonexistence remained possible, its subsequent existence would amount to the preference of one alternative without a determinant.
note: The bracketed portions in parentheses are lemmata of the matn as presented by the printed commentary; the intervening and subsequent explanation belongs to the running commentary. This passage supports the analysis of a complete causal nexus, NOT by itself a particular doctrine of secondary natural efficiency or a necessity constraining the divine will.
evidence: DIRECT PRINTED IMAGE — top running text at I:142; independent matn verification outstanding

heading: Preparatory versus strictly producing causes
category: Running commentary + lower annotations, separate voices
arabic: بأن المؤثر في وجود المعلول ليس هو العلة الفاعلية بجملتها، بل ذات الفاعل، وسائر ما يرجع إليها إنما هي شرائط التأثير
english: The productive factor in an effect’s existence is not simply the entire collection called its efficient cause: the agent itself must be distinguished from additional conditions of its efficacy.
note: A close reading of the smaller lower register of I:141 differentiates the efficient factor from its conditions. This is not a verbatim lemma of al-Taftāzānī; its specific marginal author remains to be identified. Do not turn this distinction into an explicit Sanandajī endorsement until the marginal attribution has been checked.
evidence: DIRECT PRINTED IMAGE — smaller lower register I:141; voice unassigned

heading: Angels, separate intellects, and jinn as reported theories
category: Explicitly reported claims, not authorial endorsement
arabic: (وزعموا أن الملائكة هم العقول المجردة والنفوس الفلكية) … (وزعموا) (أن الجن أرواح) هي جواهر (مجردة لها تصرف) وتأثير (في الأجسام العنصرية)
english: “They claimed that the angels are separate intellects and celestial souls” … and “they claimed that jinn are spirits,” namely substances “separate [from matter], possessing activity” and influence “upon elemental bodies.”
note: The repeated **زعموا** explicitly distances the expositor from the claims being reported. Revision 14 was correct not to attribute an endorsement of these philosophical identifications to Sanandajī. A direct image now confirms the reportative framing.
evidence: DIRECT PRINTED IMAGE — II:101 main running text

heading: Ends, wisdoms, and divine action
category: Quoted matn lemma within theological commentary
arabic: ذهب المعتزلة إلى تعليل أفعاله تعالى بالأغراض والأشاعرة إلى عدمه. (الحق أن تعليل بعض أفعاله) سيما الأحكام الشرعية كما في الحدود والكفارات وتحريم المسكرات (بالأغراض) أي الحكم الراجعة إلى العباد ظاهر (ثابت بالنص) … (والإجماع) … (وعليه مبنى) حجة (القياس)
english: The Muʿtazila maintained that God’s acts are explained by purposes, whereas the Ashʿarīs denied this. “The correct position is that the explanation of some of His acts”—especially legal rulings, such as punishments, expiations and the prohibition of intoxicants—“by purposes,” meaning wisdoms that benefit servants, is manifest and “established by revelation” and “consensus”; “upon this rests” the evidential force of “analogical reasoning.”
note: This directly verifies the earlier R12 topic, but not the exact full wording of a separately edited Tahdhīb copy. The text carefully differentiates purposes/wisdoms serving creatures from a purpose arising from lack in God. The assertion concerns some acts, NOT all acts under a universal necessitating final cause.
evidence: DIRECT PRINTED IMAGE — II:201; candidate matn words appear in parentheses

heading: The denial of benefit accruing to God
category: Running explanation plus lower marginal annotation
arabic: الغرض من التكليف … (الضرر من الثواب) … (ولا يلزم الغرض) … (وأغراض) للعباد
english: The discussion distinguishes the purposes or benefits associated with obligation and reward, while resisting the inference that a motivating need or benefit accrues to God.
note: These are selected signposts from two full pages, not a contiguous translation. The smaller marginal commentary at the bottom of both pages raises objections and qualifications; these are held under a distinct “marginal voice unassigned” label until the printed edition’s voice key is systematically audited.
evidence: DIRECT PRINTED IMAGES — II:202–203; paraphrastic digest, not continuous translation
